description: Dependency-advisory exceptions. PRODUCTION advisories are NEVER waived and this file is not consulted for them — the production tree is at zero HIGH/CRITICAL and must stay there. Only development-tree advisories may be waived, and only as an exact, evidence-backed, expiring record.
productionPolicy: zero HIGH or CRITICAL, no exceptions
developmentPolicy: zero HIGH or CRITICAL unless matched by an exact exception below: one advisory, one package, one affected range, one dependency-path fingerprint, one expiry
matchingRules: An exception matches ONLY when the advisory id, the package name, the affected range and the full set of resolved dependency nodes all agree. A different advisory, a different package, a widened range, or a changed dependency path fails the gate rather than being absorbed.
remediationRecord: At the audit baseline the PRODUCTION tree carried 3 HIGH findings covering 13 advisories: next@16.2.10 (proxy bypass, two SSRF, unauthenticated Server Function disclosure, two cache-confusion, DoS, unbounded payload, image DoS), postcss@8.4.31 (three) and sharp@0.34.5 (libvips CVEs). Resolved through compatible patch upgrades: next 16.2.10 to 16.2.12, plus overrides pinning postcss to ^8.5.24 and sharp to ^0.35.3 because Next pins postcss at exactly 8.4.31 and npm's only suggested remedy was downgrading Next to 9.3.3. Production is now at zero HIGH/CRITICAL.

removedAdvisories.removedBecause: The entry's own removalCondition fired. It read: 'The parent dependency chain supports a patched compatible brace-expansion version — that is, ... or npm reports a non-semver-major fixAvailable. When that happens the gate FAILS with a compatible-fix-available finding, because an exception that outlives its cause is worse than none.' All three of the gate's findings say the same thing from different angles: the advisory was re-scoped upstream from <=5.0.7 to <1.1.17, so only the 1.x instance remains affected; the dependency fingerprint collapsed from two nodes to one; and npm now reports fixAvailable: true with no major bump.
removedAdvisories.remediation: npm audit fix --package-lock-only bumped node_modules/minimatch/node_modules/brace-expansion from 1.1.16 to 1.1.18. Lockfile only — package.json is unchanged and NO override was added. npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities across the whole tree.
removedAdvisories.verifiedByExecution: The record warned that the previous remediation attempt (an override to ^5.0.8) broke ESLint with `TypeError: expand is not a function`, and insisted that be verified by execution rather than inferred. So this one was too: after `npm ci`, `npm run lint` is clean and the unit tier passes 1285/1285. A 1.1.x patch keeps the v1 export shape minimatch@3 calls.
removedAdvisories.note: Kept rather than deleted so the history of this waiver survives its removal. The container findings AR-35, AR-37 and AR-43 recorded in the original entry remain valuable independently of the advisory: brace-expansion CODE is still vendored inside the node binary and always will be, which is why the reachability evidence was rebuilt to assert non-reachability rather than absence. That reasoning is preserved in docs/engineering/ci-automation/evidence/brace-expansion-reachability-proof.md.
